title: MAKER predicate in delivery-gate-stop.ps1 is blind to D-042's canonical **Handshake status:** field, so a genuinely pending unit reads pend=0 and the machine-wide gate goes SILENT
evidence: delivery-gate-stop.ps1:375 matches the legacy-only anchor '(?m)^[\s\-*#>|]*Status:\s*ready-for-check'. Reproduced by the checker with the real hook in two identical throwaway trees differing only in the field name: legacy '**Status:** ready-for-check' -> BLOCK-MAKER pend=1; canonical '**Handshake status:** ready-for-check' -> MAKER pend=0 unclosed=0 queue=0 fixgap=0, no block. Same defect class as fix 4 of iss-346-round-cap-mechanical-check, which corrected it in ROUNDCAP only. Contract delivery-gate.md [C1] and [C7].
fix_direction: Two separable steps. (1) The C7 obligation, inside iss-346 fix cycle 1: state the defect-4 sibling audit result in the manifest -- disclosure, not code. (2) The code fix needs its own authorized unit: D-049 authorizes delivery-gate-stop.ps1 for the ISS-346 round-cap check, not for a second predicate, so widening MAKER's anchor to the '(?:Handshake[^\S\r\n]+)?Status:' form requires a DECISIONS entry with Approved-by. Audit mc-precommit.ps1 for the same anchor at the same time.

title: MAKER predicate reads the verdict result through Strip-Code, so a fenced PASS at the current cycle is reported as a fix gap instead of an unclosed PASS -- the block message names the wrong action on ~45% of verdicts
evidence: delivery-gate-stop.ps1:388 tests the Strip-Code'd verdict text for '^VERDICT: PASS' and falls through to $fixgap++ otherwise. Measured by the checker over this repo's real corpus: 76 of 170 verdicts (44.7%) hold a real ^VERDICT: PASS that Strip-Code destroys. Reproduced live: a manifest at Fix cycle 0 with a fenced PASS verdict at Cycle checked 0 produced 'BLOCK-MAKER pend=0 unclosed=0 queue=0 fixgap=1', where unclosed=1 is correct. Severity is medium, not high, because $backlog sums pend+unclosed+queue+fixgap, so the gate still BLOCKS -- the loud/silent direction is intact and only the instruction is wrong. This reintroduces the exact defect ISS-186 closed (the block message naming the wrong action).
fix_direction: Replace the Strip-Code'd match at line 388 with the Test-VerdictPass helper this unit already added 250 lines above it -- a one-line change, no new code. Needs its own authorizing DECISIONS entry with Approved-by (same scope argument as ISS-A035913-001). Disclosed honestly by the builder as out of D-049's scope; filed here as the checker's row, as the builder asked.

title: The ROUNDCAP cap is silently evaded by a manifest that names its seam in PROSE rather than a backticked path -- 18 of 171 real manifests are already in that shape
evidence: ROUNDCAP skips a candidate whose Seam.Count is 0 ('no extractable seam -> no claim, stay silent'), and Get-ManifestSeam only extracts path/file.ext inside backticks. Reproduced by the checker with the real hook, two identical throwaway trees with the same seam and the same two real prior PASSes, differing only in the candidate manifest's wording: (A) a backticked 'src/a/target.ts' -> BLOCKED True; (B) the same file named in prose as 'the vector target file under src/a (target.ts)' -> BLOCKED False, trace 'ROUNDCAP candidates=1 capped=0'. Independently measured: 18 of 171 manifests in this repo have no extractable seam. The trace line reads as 'checked, nothing capped', which is the false confidence ISS-346 exists to remove. The silence is deliberate in the code comment, so this is a scope limit -- but it is absent from the manifest's 'What this unit does not fix', which discloses six smaller things. Contract delivery-gate.md [I2].
fix_direction: Do not widen the seam extractor to bare basenames -- that was already measured useless (it joins unrelated units). Instead make the silence loud: when a candidate has zero extractable seam, require the manifest to carry either an extractable seam or an explicit 'Round cap:' line, rather than returning capped=0. That turns an unmeasurable unit into a decision on the record, the same mechanism the cap already uses, and keeps the fail-open property.

title: roundcap-wouldblock-census.ps1 claims its parsers are 'extracted verbatim from the live hook' but hand-copies the candidate-status regex in its pre-fix legacy-only form
evidence: qa/probes/roundcap-wouldblock-census.ps1:33 uses the legacy-only '(?m)^[\s\-*#>|]*Status:\s*ready-for-check' while the live hook at delivery-gate-stop.ps1:256 uses the '(?im)...(?:Handshake[^\S\r\n]+)?Status:' form. Four functions ARE dot-sourced verbatim out of the hook; this one regex is not, and it is exactly the defect (fix 4) the unit corrected. Materiality measured by the checker across all five census trees: 0 manifests are a live-hook candidate but not a census candidate, out of 1,021 -- so the reported blast-radius numbers stand today. Latent: a canonical-only candidate would be invisible to the census while the live hook could block on it.
fix_direction: Extract the candidate-status and Round-cap regexes out of the hook source the same way the four functions are, or drop the 'verbatim' claim from the header comment. One line either way. Medium per the repo severity gate: verify inside the next unit that touches this probe.

title: Enumerated-debt id for the iss-346 capability-coverage row T6 (bold-prefixed fields), disclosed UNVERIFIED with no admissible single-hunk falsification and carrying no issue id
evidence: qa/manifests/iss-346-round-cap-mechanical-check.md 'Capability coverage', final row: 'none is admissible -- disclosed, not faked'. The checker verified the redundancy claim rather than accepting it: Get-VerdictTokens clause 1's separator class '[^\w\r\n]{0,4}' matches ':** ' in exactly 4 characters, so dropping the emphasis strip leaves '**VERDICT:** PASS' still matching -- either mechanism alone suffices and no one-hunk edit isolates the capability. The builder measured this (reported as 'mutation falsified nothing'), then withdrew the mutation instead of dressing it up. The only defect was the missing id; this is it.
fix_direction: No code change. Either cite this id on the row, or isolate the property with a two-hunk edit in a future unit that has authorization to touch the file. The property is asserted by T6 and used as M2's control, so it is not untested -- only not mutation-covered.

title: SEVERITY CORRECTION to ISS-190: high -> critical. The verified byte state of a Stop hook firing in EVERY project on this machine is pinned by no commit in any repo, and two authorized units plus this verdict all cite it as evidence
evidence: git -C D:/ai_os diff --numstat -- .claude/hooks/delivery-gate-stop.ps1 = '224 7' (cumulative: the previous unit's change is uncommitted there too). git -C D:/ai_os status --porcelain shows FOUR modified enforcement hooks (delivery-gate-stop.ps1, aios-write-guard.ps1, edit-in-place-guard.ps1, tests/hook-fixtures.ps1) plus .claude/rules/lifecycle.md and .claude/skills/checker/SKILL.md. The verified state 5d6e0994...5162 exists only in a dirty working tree; one 'git checkout' or 'git stash' in D:/ai_os silently reverts the enforcement for d:/erp, d:/vc, d:/autoTesting, d:/vidysea/* and every scratch directory. Concurred by the checker of delivery-gate-machine-wide-fix and by this unit's builder. Recorded as an APPEND in a lane shard rather than an in-place edit of qa/issues.jsonl, per D-019: an in-place edit defeats the 'qa/issues.jsonl merge=union' attribute and two lanes have already collided on that file. The sweep's single consolidation writer owns reconciling the canonical row.
fix_direction: Commit the D:/ai_os enforcement-hook changes under their ratifying entries with a narrow pathspec, or revert them. Until then, no verdict in any project may cite a D:/ai_os fixture run as evidence without stating that the tree is dirty -- as this verdict does. What raises it to critical is not the line count but that the loss is silent, machine-wide, and reachable by an ordinary git command in an unrelated session.

title: LEDGER CORRECTION to ISS-365 reproduction 3: the prior PASSed units on the mc-sessionstart.ps1 seam are FOUR, not three -- 4 before, 5 after
evidence: ISS-365's row records 'T-017b-snapshot-features-ledger, ledger-shard-union-reader, mc-hooks-bolded-status = 3 before this unit, 4 after'. Independently measured by the checker with the live hook's Get-ManifestSeam + Test-VerdictPass over all 170 verdicts and 171 manifests: PASSed units whose manifest '## What changed' names .claude/hooks/mc-sessionstart.ps1 = 5 -- codex-hooks-links, handshake-field-reader, ledger-shard-union-reader, mc-hooks-bolded-status, T-017b-snapshot-features-ledger. Excluding the candidate (handshake-field-reader) leaves 4 priors. The omitted member is codex-hooks-links, which landed the same day and whose '## What changed, per file' names that path. The unit's probe result 'REFUSED: True (4 prior PASS(es))' is therefore right, and its hard-coded prior list is right; the ledger row is wrong. fix_direction: Reconcile ISS-365's reproduction 3 to '4 before, 5 after' with codex-hooks-links added, via the sweep's consolidation writer (append, not in-place edit, per D-019). D-015 measures a fix against its issue's own recorded reproductions, so an id-to-row mismatch here would mis-measure the next cycle.

title: The checked-PASS iss-346 manifest on master carries, as a COVERED capability row, the last-VERDICT-line ordering rule that its own cycle-1 verdict rejects as a regression and that the live hook deliberately does not implement
evidence: master:qa/manifests/iss-346-round-cap-mechanical-check.md line 298 presents 'The operative verdict is the LAST VERDICT: line, so a superseded PASS is not a round' as a capability with a GREEN-before/RED-after falsification (C4) behind it, and that manifest is checked-PASS at 97756f5. Its cycle-1 verdict supersedes it only in prose (it FAILed cycle 0 on that very premise, calls applying it 'reintroducing, not fixing, a real regression on the newest-first-archive' shape, and marks C4 'legitimately superseded'). Measured by the checker: the live hook at sha256 5d6e0994...5162 implements the cumulative any-PASS rule and contains no $vLast last-line gate. Decisive test: feeding master's own PASS verdict file (newest-first, '# ARCHIVE -- cycle 0 verdict (FAIL)' at line 299) to the live parsers gives tokens PASS@77 then twelve later tokens ending FAIL@16941 -- the cumulative rule reads True (correct), the LAST-line rule reads FAIL (wrong). A PASSed unit's own verdict is misread by the rule its manifest still advertises.
fix_direction: Amend the PASSed manifest's capability table to mark that row withdrawn, citing its own cycle-1 verdict, so a future unit reading it for precedent cannot reintroduce an under-counting cap into a machine-wide hook. No code change: the hook is already correct. Medium because the trap lives in the audit record, which is exactly what the next unit reads as ground truth.

title: The iss-346 cycle-1 [C7] audit never mentions the two sibling hooks the contract names as in-scope, and one of them (mc-precommit.ps1) has a live, undisclosed instance of the same canonical-field blindness the unit fixed in ROUNDCAP
evidence: qa/contracts/delivery-gate.md 'Artifacts under contract' explicitly names mc-sessionstart.ps1 and mc-precommit.ps1 as in-scope 'because they share the predicate', and [C7] requires an audit across 'every predicate and every sibling hook that shares the pattern'. The cycle-1 manifest's Cross-predicate audit section states 'ROUNDCAP and MAKER are the only two predicates in delivery-gate-stop.ps1 ... So MAKER is the only sibling this audit needs to cover' -- addressing only predicates inside one file and never mentioning either contract-named hook. Checked independently by the checker: mc-sessionstart.ps1:62 reads verdicts via Select-String (no Strip-Code), so it is genuinely unaffected by defect 1, and mc-sessionstart.ps1:35 already reads the canonical **Handshake status:** field, so it is unaffected by defect 4 -- a legitimate 'checked, not affected' the manifest could have stated but omitted entirely. mc-precommit.ps1:43's pending-unit regex '^\s*(?:[-*]\s+)?(?:#{1,6}\s+)?[*_]{0,3}Status:[*_]{0,3}\s+ready-for-check' requires the literal substring Status: at the anchored position; verified with the real regex against both forms: legacy '**Status:** ready-for-check' matches True, canonical-only '**Handshake status:** ready-for-check' matches False. So a manifest written to the current canonical standard is silently excluded from mc-precommit's pre-commit WARN count -- the identical defect-4 class, live, in a third contract-named artifact, unaudited and undisclosed.
fix_direction: State mc-sessionstart.ps1 as checked-not-affected in the C7 section (both sub-defects). File the mc-precommit.ps1 gap as its own [C7]/[C1] instance and gate its fix the same way as ISS-A035913-001 -- add the '(?:Handshake[^\S\r\n]+)?' alternation at line 43, mirroring D-042's ROUNDCAP form. Unlike delivery-gate-stop.ps1, mc-precommit.ps1 is repo-local (D:/KnowledgeBase/.claude/hooks/), so this fix is NOT blocked by ISS-190's cross-repo commit problem and could be authorized and shipped in this repo alone once the Approver rules on qa/gates/maker-predicate-canonical-field-and-prose-seam.md or a narrower follow-up gate.
